chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man confesses upon himself with a penalty (Hadd) or a fabrication, then denies it, he is whipped.
I said, 'What is your view if he confesses with a penalty (Hadd) upon himself, in which stoning is reached, would you have him stoned?'
He said, 'No. But, I would have whipped him.'

key_terms.حَدّ: A fixed penalty prescribed by Sharia for a specific crime

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for someone who confesses to a crime and then denies it?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural distinction between the penalty for the crime itself and the penalty for the subsequent denial (Jahd) after confession. He specifies that even for major crimes like adultery carrying Rajm (stoning), the immediate consequence of denying the confession is flogging (Jald), rather than executing the full Hadd penalty, highlighting the principle that denial does not automatically trigger the full corporal punishment associated with the crime. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view on the efficacy of confession and the specific legal consequences of retracting it.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the man accepts upon himself with a Penalty (Hadd), or fabrication, then denies it, would be whipped’.
I said, ‘What is your view that if he accepts with a Penalty (Hadd) upon himself, in which stoning is reached, would youasws have him stoned?’
He <sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No. But, I<sup>asws</sup> would have whipped him’.
